original_value: Brain-computer interface (BCI) systems translate the human neurophysiological activities into commands through EEG analysis. Improving the BCI performances leads to faster and easier use and less fatigue. In this study, we proposed a new prepossessing approach to increase the robustness of a steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) based BCI. Inspiring from the known properties of the SSVEP frequency components, the goal was to enhance the signal quality by making it more convenient to be interpreted by the decision-making step. We first investigated the potential to detect the deteriorating periods based on the physiological properties of the SSVEP. The proposed system localizes the intervals which can obscure the SSVEP frequencies by a new algorithm founded on the processing and the analysis of the instantaneous phase. The piecewise linear regression allows a sampler comprehension of the phase signal. Then, these intervals are filtered by the moving average filter to enhance the SSVEP quality. Finally, the decision making is made by the canonical correlation analysis (CCA) algorithm. The results of experiments, using real EEG signals from five subjects, show that the proposed approach significantly increases the performances in terms of accuracy and information transfer rate by about 7.3% and 3.85 bits/min, respectively, in case of 2 s segment length. On the other hand, the spatial filtering methods of the literature weaken the system performances.

result.paraphrase: Brain-computer interface (BCI) systems convert human neurophysiological activity into commands by analyzing EEG signals. Better BCI performance enables quicker, simpler use with less fatigue. In this study, we proposed a new preprocessing method to improve the robustness of a steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based BCI. Drawing on the known properties of SSVEP frequency components, the aim was to improve signal quality so that the decision-making stage could interpret it more easily. First, we examined the possibility of detecting deteriorating periods based on the physiological characteristics of SSVEP. The proposed system identifies intervals that may obscure SSVEP frequencies using a new algorithm based on instantaneous phase processing and analysis. Piecewise linear regression provides a simpler understanding of the phase signal. These intervals are then filtered with a moving average filter to enhance SSVEP quality. Finally, the decision is made using the canonical correlation analysis (CCA) algorithm. Experiments with real EEG signals from five subjects show that the proposed approach significantly improves performance in accuracy and information transfer rate by about 7.3% and 3.85 bits/min, respectively, for a 2 s segment length. By contrast, the spatial filtering methods in the literature reduce system performance.
